cells.tense: Right now you are open to what is actually here, and you are letting the moment stay fresh.
cells.ask: Before the day ends, write down one possibility you are holding and the next step you could take with it — then take that step within the week.
cells.core:
You are standing where nothing has been decided yet, and you are not treating that as a problem. People who land here usually rush to pick something so the openness stops. You have not. You can hold what you might do alongside what is actually in front of you, adjusting as the day moves, and still stay in the room you are in.

That is rare enough that it can look like doing nothing. It is not. The next thing is already asking for you, and you have something to feed it. Pick the possibility you have been carrying the longest alongside the one that arrived today. Put one next to the other and let the next step show itself.
cells.sheetLine: You are still open, and you get to point that somewhere.
cells.verb: holding everything open before it is chosen
cells.place: where you keep adjusting to stay in flow

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead of you there is a version where all of this is finally settled, and you are already living there.
cells.ask: Choose one path you are holding open and take a visible step on it this week — then let the other paths be what they are for now.
cells.core:
You keep the options alive because closing one feels like losing the rest. So the room stays full of versions of your life, and none of them gets your weight. You are watching for a sign that one is safe to land on, and the sign keeps not coming, because the thing that would tell you is the landing itself.

What you are protecting is real, and that protection has a cost. Nothing about them is gone when you pick one. They sit exactly where they sit, and you can come back. Stand on one thing this week and let the rest stay open. Then see what the ground is actually like under it.
cells.sheetLine: You are waiting to be sure before you land, and the sure keeps not coming.
cells.verb: holding everything open before it is chosen

cells.tense: You are still standing in a doorway from a while back, and the room on the other side has already moved on without you.
cells.ask: Step outside your own view and describe one pattern you are in, to yourself, on paper — then choose one thing in it you could do differently.
cells.core:
Something in a past room made being open feel unsafe, and you have been carrying that lesson in your body. You still know how to stand before an undecided moment. What is missing is the willingness to stand in it — you stay just outside, and the moment goes by without you.

This is not a lack of possibility. There is plenty of it, and you can feel it when you are not busy keeping it at arm's length. What would open the door is not pushing yourself to feel more. It is seeing the whole pattern — including the room you are still in — from enough distance to name it. That kind of seeing is available right now, and it does not need you to relive anything.
cells.sheetLine: You are standing outside your own life, and it is already happening without you.
cells.verb: holding everything open before it is chosen

cells.tense: You are already moving through this, adjusting as you go, and you keep describing it as if it were just how things are.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have been calling 'the situation' and describe it as a choice you are making — out loud, once, to someone.
cells.core:
Watch yourself in a moment that does not go the way you expected. Something adjusts, quickly, without a rehearsal — you have already changed your approach before you notice you did it. That is you doing it. You call it being realistic, or just the way things are, and in both cases the moving is happening and the saying-so has not caught up.

There are more doors in front of you than you are seeing, not because they are hidden but because you have been reading the moment as fixed. It is not fixed. It is being shaped, and you are one of the shapers. Take one thing you have been calling the situation and say out loud that it is a choice. That is the whole ask, and it is small enough to do today.
cells.sheetLine: You are steering this without saying so, and there is room you have not used.
